correlation_vs_official_margin.interpretation: nflverse spread_line is documented as "positive = home team favoured". Correlating it against the official home margin tests that convention on this season. A strong positive r confirms positive = home favoured.

sign_convention.reason: It is the only reading consistent with the documented convention (positive = home favoured), it produces a plausible push count, and it reproduces a push on the Week 1 NE@SEA game (spread 3, home won by exactly 3). The 0.41 home cover rate it yields for 2026 is a real season effect, not a convention error: the market has been pricing home teams ~1.6 points richer than the official results justify.

spread_vs_home_moneyline.reading: A strong NEGATIVE r means a larger positive spread goes with a shorter (more negative) home price, i.e. positive spread = home favoured.

decisive_single_game.conclusion: The home price is -166, so the home team is the favourite. The spread is +3 and the home team won by exactly 3. A 3-point favourite winning by exactly 3 is a push, which fixes the convention: the home side covers when the official home margin exceeds +3.
